name: Ptosis fixing with Muller muscle resection

image.caption: Ptosis fixing with Muller muscle resection

lead: Muller muscle resection is a surgical way to correct blepharoptosis, a drooping upper eyelid. The surgeon shortens Muller's muscle, a small muscle that helps hold the lid up, so the lid sits higher and the eye looks more open.

A raised lid can make a face look more awake and attractive. In a 2025 observer study of ptosis surgery patients, including those who had Muller muscle resection, masked raters scored photos for attractiveness, success and health.

paras: It is performed by an oculoplastic or eyelid surgeon, usually under local anesthesia with or without sedation. Studies have compared nerve-block and subconjunctival anesthesia and the effect of adding epinephrine. Healing is followed over weeks.

Risks of ptosis surgery in general include asymmetry, dry eye, bleeding, infection and, rarely, loss of lid movement; some patients need repeat surgery. A surgeon decides which technique suits the individual.

chain: Eyes look more open and alert
angle.text: The surgery raises a drooping upper lid, which opens the eye and changes the overall expression. Observer studies of ptosis surgery assess perceived attractiveness, success and health.

lead: Ptosis surgery with Muller muscle resection treats a drooping upper eyelid by shortening Muller's muscle, an option among several ptosis procedures that also include levator resection and frontalis slings [1][2]. Many patients present for functional reasons such as blocked vision, and the procedure also changes appearance.

The appearance payoff is a raised upper lid that opens the eye. A systematic review of 28 papers found Muller muscle resection raised the marginal reflex distance by about 2.0 mm on average, compared with 1.8 mm for levator resection, 2.3 mm for aponeurotic surgery and 2.4 mm for frontalis suspension [3]. Patients in the Muller group were older on average, around 59 years [3].

A 2025 study had masked observers rate faces before or after ptosis surgery (levator resection and Muller muscle resection) for attractiveness, success and health on 0-100 scales [4]. Other trials in the conjunctival Muller approach have examined pain control and anesthetic choice [5][6].

paras: Ptosis surgery options include levator resection, Muller muscle resection and frontalis sling. The choice depends on lid-lift strength and other findings [2]. Surgeons in studies of the conjunctival approach compared frontal nerve blocks with subconjunctival anesthesia [5] and anesthetic with and without epinephrine [6].

A review of 28 papers reported mean lid-margin improvement of 2.0 mm for Muller resection [3]. In one general ptosis source, half of patients treated earlier needed more surgery within 8 to 10 years [2]. A study examined tear oxidative stress after the procedure [7].
Reported risks in ptosis surgery include asymmetry, dry eye, bleeding, infection and rare loss of lid movement [2].
Studies include the review of lid-height outcomes [3], the observer-rating study [4] and randomized anesthesia trials [5][6].
